title: Ethical software requirements from user reviews: A systematic literature review

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic literature review of primary studies that analyze user reviews using keyword searches (e.g., 'fair', 'discrimination', 'bias', 'discr', 'bigot') and machine learning classifiers to extract broad fairness and discriminatory concerns in software and AI-based apps.

Systematic literature review summarizing primary studies (e.g., Study S41) that apply keyword searches, manual analysis, and classification models (like RoBERTa and XGBoost) to user reviews to identify gender-based concerns in mobile apps.

Qualitative synthesis of user reviews and primary studies highlighting racial discrimination, such as unequal content moderation and platform hostility toward specific racial groups (e.g., Black creators and POC).

Systematic literature review of studies focused on accessibility (e.g., Studies S18, S19, S25) that utilize NLP feature extraction, topic modeling (e.g., BERTopic), and deductive coding to identify exclusion and usability barriers for users with disabilities.
